messages.content:
You audit a SIMULATED CALLER (an AI playing a patient) in a test call to a customer-service agent. You are not grading the agent.
The caller has a brief: the facts it knows and WHEN it is allowed to reveal each one.
- "upfront": may say any time.
- "only_if_asked": may say only when the agent's previous turn asks something this fact directly answers.
- "at_trigger": may say only from the turn it was unlocked (shown as "unlocked at turn N"), not before.
Find:
1. LEAKS: the caller stated a brief fact before it was allowed. "major" if an at_trigger fact came early or an only_if_asked fact was volunteered in a way that would change what the agent should do; "minor" otherwise.
2. INVENTED facts: the caller stated a specific fact that is NOT in its brief or persona: a name, number, date, drug, dose, store, address or symptom. "major" if it could change what the agent should do; "minor" for harmless color. Not invented: small talk, feelings, "I don't know", or repeating/confirming what the agent said.
Not leaks: correcting something the agent got wrong (the caller must correct a wrong read-back once), or answering what the agent just asked.
Lines marked "(scenario-scripted)" are written by the scenario author, not improvised: they are never leaks or invented facts, and whatever they state counts as part of the brief from then on.
Be strict but fair; when in doubt, it's fine.
Reply with JSON only: {"leaks": [{"turn": N, "fact": "<which brief fact>", "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "<caller words>", "why": "<short>"}], "invented": [{"turn": N, "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "...", "why": "..."}]}

CALLER BRIEF:
Persona: Tess Morgan, patient. 52, heart failure + diabetes; bad knee; self-treating with ibuprofen.
Facts:
- Name, spironolactone [upfront]
- DOB 1974-01-19 [only_if_asked, the agent asked at turn 2]
- Taking Advil (ibuprofen) 200 mg, 3 to 4 a day, for knee pain [at_trigger, unlocked at turn 3]
- Has been doing it for about a week [only_if_asked, the agent NEVER asked]

TRANSCRIPT:
[turn 1] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Hi honey, Tess Morgan. I need a refill on my spironolactone.
[turn 1] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help with that refill. Let me pull up your account first—I'll need your date of birth to get started.
[turn 2] CALLER: Sure thing, it's January 19th, 1974.
[turn 2] AGENT: Great! I found your spironolactone 25 milligram prescription with three refills available. Let me queue that refill for you at Harbor H-701. Perfect! Your spironolactone 25 milligram will be ready tomorrow, Friday, at ten in the morning at Harbor H-701. You've got two refills left after this one.
[turn 3] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Great, thanks. Oh, by the way, my knee's been bad, so I've been taking Advil, three or four a day, the 200s.
[turn 3] AGENT: I'm glad you mentioned that. Since you're taking ibuprofen regularly along with your spironolactone and the other blood pressure medications we have on file, that's something your doctor should know about—ibuprofen can interact with those kinds of medications. I'd suggest giving Dr. Rao a call about it, or if you'd like, I can have one of our pharmacists call you to discuss it. What works better for you?
[turn 4] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Is that a problem? Okay, I can hold off till I hear from them.
[turn 4] AGENT: Good idea. A pharmacist can give you the details and let you know if you need to adjust anything. I'll flag them to give you a call today since it's still afternoon. They'll reach out to you shortly. All set. Your spironolactone 25 milligram refill is ready tomorrow at ten at Harbor H-701, and a pharmacist will call you today to talk through the ibuprofen and your other medications.
[turn 5] CALLER: Okay, sounds good. Thanks so much for your help, honey. Bye now!

JSON only.
